name: Mornington Winter Music Festival
tagline: A long-weekend music crawl through Mornington’s venues and Main Street.
summary: Mornington Winter Music Festival turns the King’s Birthday long weekend into a town-wide music program, with gigs across bars, restaurants, churches and theatres plus street entertainment along Main Street. It is Mornington’s winter counterpoint to the Peninsula wine-country weekend happening at the same time.
heroImageAlt: Mornington foreshore and town centre near Main Street
whatItIs:
A multi-day winter music program spread across Mornington venues and the Main Street precinct. The program has included jazz, blues, soul, R&B and related styles, with ticketed venue gigs sitting beside free or low-cost street entertainment. The exact venue map changes by year, which is part of the appeal: the festival functions like a town crawl rather than a single fenced event.

For visitors, the smart way to use it is to pick one or two sessions, book a meal around them, and let the rest of the night stay loose. Trying to treat the whole program as a completion exercise misses the point.
whoItsFor: Music lovers, Mornington locals, winter-weekend visitors and couples who want something more structured than dinner but less demanding than a full festival pass. It suits people happy to move between venues and weather-proof a winter night. Families can use the street program where available, but many venue gigs are better suited to adults.
peninsulaCalendarContext: Runs in the same long-weekend window as Winter Wine Weekend, giving the bay-side town of Mornington its own winter reason to travel while the wine country is busy around Red Hill and Main Ridge. It broadens the Peninsula’s winter identity beyond cellar doors and hot springs.
gettingThere: Base yourself in Mornington if you can: the practical advantage is being able to walk between Main Street venues without moving the car. From Melbourne, allow roughly 60–75 minutes in normal traffic. Check the program before booking dinner, since the best evening is usually built around venue location rather than headline name alone.
